payload.title: Travel Advisor Benefits You Cannot Get Booking Alone
payload.excerpt: You can book a flight in minutes. A destination wedding is something else: flights, villas, a venue, a photographer, guests arriving from three cities and deposits due in two currencies.
key_takeaways: A good travel advisor gives you one point of contact across flights, stays and the wedding itself.
Ask for quotes in Australian dollars and for every inclusion in writing before you commit.
Plenty of couples book their own flights and stays, but the harder parts are guests, many suppliers and payments in several currencies.
Before you agree, ask any advisor about their fee in writing, inclusions, cancellation terms, insolvency cover and travel insurance.

faq.q: What does a travel advisor do?
faq.a: A travel advisor plans and books travel on your behalf, and coordinates the separate bookings so dates, deposits and terms line up. For a destination wedding, that can extend to the venue, travel and suppliers.

faq.q: Is a travel advisor worth it for a destination wedding?
faq.a: It depends on how much there is to hold together. If you have guests, several suppliers and payments in more than one currency, an advisor saves you the coordination. If it is a simple trip for two, you may manage comfortably yourself. Your consumer guarantees are the same either way.

faq.q: Can I book some things myself and use an advisor for the rest?
faq.a: Yes. Many couples book their own flights or honeymoon stays and hand over the wedding pieces. Tell your advisor what you have booked, so dates and deposits can be planned around it.

faq.q: Do travel advisors quote in Australian dollars?
faq.a: Ask before you start. Overseas suppliers charge in their own currency, and the exchange rate and fees vary between providers. A quote in AUD, with the inclusions in writing, lets you compare options on the same footing.

faq.q: What should I ask before hiring a travel advisor?
faq.a: Ask how the fee is charged and whether it is in writing, what each quote includes, what the cancellation and change terms are for the advisor and each provider, whether they hold insolvency insurance, and how overseas payments are made. Then arrange travel insurance early.
